app.title: StemCell Fate Explorer
app.summary: The person opens a dashboard that reads cell-level results already computed by a separate analysis script: an embedding, state labels, pseudotime, fate probabilities and gene–fate associations. If those files are missing, it stops and explains how to make them. They start with an overview of counts, the embedding coloured by state and how many cells fall in each state. Then they recolour the embedding by state, pseudotime or differentiation potential, and pick a terminal fate to see each cell's probability of reaching it, with a table of that probability per state. Last, they rank the genes most associated with a chosen fate and download the list as CSV, or pick one gene to see its expression on the embedding, along pseudotime and per state.

task.text: Explore model-inferred cell fate probabilities over a single-cell atlas and pull out the genes most associated with each terminal fate.

data.text: Precomputed per-cell tables (embedding coordinates, state label, pseudotime, probability of reaching each terminal fate, expression of selected marker genes), a ranked table of gene–fate associations with statistics, and run metadata.
data.item: a single cell with its state label, embedding coordinates, pseudotime and its probability of reaching each terminal fate

stage.text: exploring the fate-model output of a single-cell analysis pipeline, before experimental validation

mechanism.text: A sidebar switches between pages. Each page shows the same 2-D cell embedding as a scatter plot, recoloured by whatever the person picks (state, pseudotime, one fate's probability, one gene's expression), next to bar charts and tables that sum that quantity up by cell state. The driver page ranks genes for a fate, cuts the list with a top-N slider and exports it as CSV.

field.text: trajectory and fate-probability inference on single-cell RNA-seq in computational biology

workflow.name: map each item's probability of reaching each outcome and export the features most associated with an outcome

steps.here: Loads five precomputed files (cells, fate probabilities, driver genes, marker expression, metadata) and keeps only the cell ids found in all of them. If a file is missing, it stops and shows the command that makes the outputs.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Overview shows counts of cells, genes, states and terminal fates, a UMAP coloured by state, and a horizontal bar chart of cells per state.

steps.step: toggle what the overview is coloured by
steps.here: The Cell Atlas switches between UMAP and t-SNE (when present) and colours the cells by state, pseudotime or differentiation potential.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The Fate Map takes one terminal fate, colours every cell by its probability of reaching it, and tables the mean, median and count of that probability for each state, sorted by mean.

steps.step: rank features by association with one outcome
steps.here: Putative Drivers picks a lineage, uses a slider to keep the top 10–60 genes by correlation, and shows them as a bar chart plus a table of p-values, q-values and confidence intervals.
The Gene Explorer picks one marker gene and shows its expression on the UMAP, as a scatter against pseudotime coloured by state, and as a table of median expression per state.
A download button saves the selected lineage's top driver genes as a CSV named after that lineage.

distinctive: Every cell has a probability for each of several terminal fates, so the same embedding is recoloured fate by fate, not by one label.
A pseudotime ordering comes with the data, so a gene's expression can be plotted along inferred developmental time as well as on the embedding.
The dashboard never recomputes the model. It only reads outputs from a separate pipeline script and refuses to show placeholder results when they are missing.
Very small p-values that underflow to zero are shown as "<1e-300", and the genes are labelled putative associations, not causal regulators.
